current_limitations.assessment: Current Korean reads naturally, but the user’s 2026-10-25 foreign-word-preservation rule favors retaining 오케이. This does not imply that the older translation ignored a rule that did not yet exist.
Meaning is broadly retained; the chosen foreign word is not. Existing patch better preserves this particular feature.
The original momentary polite self-introduction is smoothed into casual speech. Surrounding casual speech can justify the choice, so this is a nuance loss rather than a proven relationship error.

current_limitations.assessment: The current first-half pronunciation note attempts to preserve the pun, but the paper-side homophone remains unclear in Korean. Neither version fully carries the wordplay in the inspected context.
Current wording is smoother but narrows an intentionally abstract shared-dead metaphor to longing. A stylistic/interpretive tradeoff, not counted as a definite mistranslation.
